extracted.intended_audience: researchers, DOE stakeholders, institutions and the general public interested in DOE energy research funding
extracted.subtask_description: A Department of Energy press release announcing $100 million in funding for 10 Energy Frontier Research Centers (EFRCs), describing selection method, program goals, team composition, research areas, expected outcomes, and award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection method: competitive peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The current cohort of EFRCs was selected by competitive peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centers were chosen through competitive peer review; favorable peer review evaluations supported renewals and two-year extensions to complete valuable research in progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition: multidisciplinary, multi-institutional teams
rubrics_metrics.description: EFRCs bring together researchers from multiple disciplines and institutions—including universities, national laboratories, industry, and nonprofit organizations—and combine them into synergistic, highly productive teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program recognizes the importance of teams in energy research and emphasizes multidisciplinary collaboration as an exemplary vehicle for forging strong teams capable of addressing complex, cross-cutting scientific and technological challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with DOE mission: accelerate breakthroughs for a 21st-century energy economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should accelerate the scientific breakthroughs needed to build a twenty-first-century energy economy and strengthen U.S. economic leadership and energy security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals/centers are framed around accelerating discovery and understanding in energy-relevant fields, and generating foundational knowledge that leads to innovations in electronics, computing, communication, quantum information sciences, chemical production from waste plastics, and nuclear waste remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research focus areas: energy-relevant science and technology domains
rubrics_metrics.description: EFRCs will accelerate scientific discovery and understanding in energy-relevant fields listed by DOE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly mentioned areas include materials and chemistry for microelectronics and quantum information science; chemical upcycling of polymers; environmental management; advanced solar energy; energy generation and storage; and nuclear energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected outputs and impact: publications, inventions, and technology transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The EFRC program is expected to generate foundational scientific knowledge, peer-reviewed publications, inventions, and technologies that benefit the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 2009 the EFRCs have produced more than 12,600 peer-reviewed publications and generated hundreds of inventions at various stages of the patent process, fostering technologies that have benefited both large and small private sector companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award terms and funding amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The program provides multi-year funding with specified average award levels and contingency on appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The average annual award for each four-year center is approximately $3 million, with lower levels of funding for two-year extensions. Total planned funding for the 10 centers is $100 million over four years, with out-year funding contingent on Congressional appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal and extension policy tied to peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewals and short-term extensions are granted based on favorable peer review evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The current cohort includes six new centers and renewals of two existing ones to be funded for up to four years; an additional two existing centers were awarded two-year extensions based on favorable peer review evaluations to support completion of valuable research in progress.
